P0.finding: The M505 arithmetic result is valid, but the prior permanent RTL kill generalized a development capture-efficiency gate into a DATE comparison gate. M505 misses the M473 concurrent-1R1W opportunity ceiling by 11.6210%, while retaining 1.746753x versus M468 strong-zero and 1.741232x versus same-coordinate bit under the frozen 240 KiB/128 B-per-cycle coordinate. M473 physical scratch PPA is explicitly open, so distance to it cannot be the sole reason to kill a realizable 1RW point.
P0.required_action: Replace the permanent kill with the bounded M528 same-ledger contract and allow at most one dead-write-only 1RW RTL candidate if its CPU gates pass.

P1.finding: M505 reports generated scratch area but does not publish a fully substituted 240 KiB capacity total. Replacing the nominal 64x1152-bit 9 KiB item with nine physical 128x128-bit generated macros and adding one conservative bitmap slice gives 213376 bytes, which still fits 245760 bytes with 32384 bytes margin.
P1.required_action: The new ledger must enumerate every memory item and fail if matcher/directory/queue metadata creates an omitted capacity obligation.

P1.finding: The 1.74x values are CPU cycle-model results. Matcher, scheduler, generated 1RW macros, response queue, resident-psum boundary, complete constraints, power, and Formality have not been closed together.
P1.required_action: Use total-area throughput efficiency and macro-inclusive energy gates before physical or paper admission.

P1.finding: M505 dead-write-only still moves 30457108224 logical parent-scratch bytes across eight output blocks. The 40.19% access reduction is relative to M504 parent scratch only, not total SRAM/DRAM traffic or energy.
P1.required_action: Price every read/write with generated-macro energy and keep the fixed 9069207552 weight DRAM bytes visible.

P1.finding: The evidence population is one DSEC sequence with ten samples and four bottleneck Conv operators, not decoder-complete or multi-sequence system performance.
P1.required_action: Keep all M505 numbers local until later system and sequence gates.

P2.finding: Project documents use 1R1W for a concurrent read-plus-write obligation and 1RW for a single read-XOR-write port. Any shortened table label can silently erase the distinction.
P2.required_action: Spell out concurrent-1R1W versus single-port-1RW in every table and caption.

P2.finding: Combined PVRF and dead-write-only are cycle-identical. The combined mode removes only 244346 further one-block writes, 0.9242% of dead-write-only accesses.
P2.required_action: Implement dead-write-only, not combined PVRF, in the one allowed RTL variant.
